articles.title: Year ago, 32 trucks with Rs 4cr rice left MP's Katni for Indore, yet to reach; probe ordered into missing consignments weighing over 1,000 quintals and possible diversion
articles.body: Key Highlights1. 32 trucks carrying over 1,000 quintals of rice, valued at Rs 4 crore, reportedly left Katni for Indore, Harda and Neemuch in 2025 but remain unaccounted for.2. The discrepancy emerged when MP State Civil Supplies Corporation matched paddy transportation records with records maintained by the beneficiary districts.3. The transporter claims all 32 consignments were delivered, but officials have found no records confirming their receipt.4. Investigators are examining whether the rice was delivered, rejected over quality issues, diverted or left unaccounted for, with possible pilferage also suspected.5. Food and Civil Supplies Minister Govind Singh Rajput has ordered a probe and sought a detailed report within seven days, warning of criminal prosecution against those found responsible.BHOPAL: Even Sherlock Holmes might have been intrigued. But maybe not, if you consider this: What are the chances of 32 rice-laden trucks setting out from MP's Katni for Indore, Harda and Neemuch - 544, 457 and 856 km, respectively, from the point of origin and not reaching their destinations in more than a year?Curiously, it's a question that nobody bothered to ask until officials of Madhya Pradesh State Civil Supplies Corporation recently matched 2025 paddy transportation records with those of the beneficiary districts, sources said.The "untraceable" consignments, exceeding 1,000 quintals, are valued at Rs 4 crore. State food and civil supplies minister Govind Singh Rajput ordered an investigation this week by a team of senior officials from Bhopal and asked additional chief secretary (food) KC Gupta to submit a detailed report within seven days.The minister said any official found responsible for negligence or suspected pilferage would be liable for criminal prosecution. The official transporter, whose identity hasn't been disclosed, apparently maintains that all 32 consignments were delivered. But with no records available to confirm that Indore, Harda and Neemuch received the rice, officials are trying to establish whether these consignments were delivered, rejected, diverted or just remained unaccounted for in the records.The investigation will cover the entire transportation chain and fix accountability for the missing stock, they said. Sources said they do not rule out a conspiracy, including diversion of foodgrain and its sale elsewhere.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: Watch: FedEx aircraft runs off runway at Miami airport on eve of Thanksgiving
articles.summary: A FedEx cargo aircraft overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, forcing the temporary closure of all but one runway and
articles.body: A FedEx cargo aircraft overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, forcing the temporary closure of all but one runway and disrupting flight operations on the eve of Thanksgiving.There were no immediate reports of injuries in the incident, which occurred around 8:40 pm, the airport said. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the scene.The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 was arriving from Memphis when it ran off the runway. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said flights were expected to resume shortly and that it would investigate the incident.The airport urged passengers scheduled to travel on Wednesday night to check with their airlines for the latest flight updates before heading to the airport."We appreciate our passengers' patience as we work to safely resume normal operations," the airport said in a statement.The incident comes nearly three months after an Amazon cargo aircraft overran another runway at the airport in September, killing five people on the ground. Although Wednesday's incident involved a different runway, three of Miami International Airport's runways converge at the western end, leaving the FedEx aircraft close to the site of the earlier crash.In the September incident, the Amazon plane veered across a road and struck a van carrying an aircraft cleaning crew.The FedEx aircraft was an MD-11, the same model involved in a deadly UPS cargo plane crash in Kentucky last year. In that incident, an engine detached from the aircraft during takeoff, killing three pilots and 12 people on the ground.The FAA subsequently approved Boeing's proposed fix for the aircraft, and FedEx resumed operating its MD-11 fleet in May.The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said it had no information about Wednesday's incident.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' gets a new OTT release date: Check out when and where to watch Shobhinaw Satyaa and Chandan Anand's devotional drama
articles.summary: 'Hanuman Ansh', a biographical devotional drama based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, is set to stream soon.
articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh', a biographical devotional drama based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, is set to stream soon. The streaming platform announced the release date and the languages in which the film will be available. This development follows Sony LIV's earlier announcement of November 27 as the film's premiere date. Another platform has now confirmed that viewers can watch the title two days later.OTT platform announces 'Hanuman Ansh' release dateNetflix shared the streaming update through its social media channels. The film will be available in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam and Gujarati starting November 29. Announcing its arrival, the platform wrote, "Faith changed his life. His devotion changed thousands. Experience the divine story of Lord Hanuman's devout disciple, now on Netflix. Watch Hanuman Ansh, out November 29 in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam and Gujarati, on Netflix India."Directed by Dr Vishal Chaturvedi, 'Hanuman Ansh' is inspired by his book 'Divine Detour: That Changed My Life'. The film presents a biographical account centred on Neem Karoli Baba, a spiritual figure whose life and teachings form the basis of the narrative. Shobhinaw Satyaa and Chandan Anand play the lead roles.The story introduces Lakshman Das as a young boy dealing with his mother's death. The personal tragedy leaves him searching for answers and a deeper understanding of life. His quest gradually develops into a spiritual journey, eventually bringing him closer to Neem Karoli Baba. By beginning with the character's grief, the film establishes an emotional connection before exploring his association with the spiritual leader.Film focuses on compassion and serviceBeyond its devotional elements, 'Hanuman Ansh' emphasises the everyday values associated with spirituality. The narrative highlights feeding people who are hungry, helping those facing difficulties and serving others without expecting anything in return. These acts of kindness form an important part of the film's message.The story presents compassion and selfless service as meaningful expressions of faith. This approach also gives the biographical drama an emotional dimension that extends beyond its portrayal of spiritual experiences and extraordinary events.ETimes gives 'Hanuman Ansh' 3.5 starsETimes rated 'Hanuman Ansh' 3.5 out of 5 stars. The review appreciated the film's sincerity and its decision to focus on Neem Karoli Baba's philosophy rather than portraying him solely through miraculous incidents. It also highlighted the importance the narrative gives to compassion and service.The review read, "Where Hanuman Ansh succeeds is in its sincerity. It doesn't try to turn Neem Karoli Baba into a larger-than-life cinematic hero, nor does it depend entirely on miracles to establish his spiritual stature. Instead, it finds greater value in the everyday acts of compassion that defined his philosophy. The film's most resonant thought is that serving humanity can itself be an expression of faith.The ETimes review also discussed the aspects that prevent the film from becoming a more engaging biographical drama. Its episodic storytelling and measured pace affect the overall viewing experience. However, the conviction behind its central message and Shobhinaw Satyaa's understated performance lend the film emotional warmth.The review further observed, "The result is a film that is emotionally sincere but not always dramatically compelling. Its measured pace and episodic structure prevent it from becoming a fully immersive biographical drama, but the conviction behind its message and Shobhinaw Satyaa's understated performance give it considerable warmth."

articles.title: Gene Autry’s missing guitar resurfaces in Sweden nearly a century later after a woman almost sells her inherited instrument for 500 kronor before its identity is confirmed
articles.summary: A guitar once owned by country music star Gene Autry has resurfaced in rural Sweden, almost a century after it was believed to have been stolen.
articles.body: A guitar once owned by country music star Gene Autry has resurfaced in rural Sweden, almost a century after it was believed to have been stolen. Sandra discovered the instrument among her late father's belongings in Gullspång in 2021. She was close to selling it for 500 kronor before a potential buyer urged her to get it valued.The guitar expert who examined it recognised it as a rare Martin OM-45 made in the early 1930s. According to Göteborgs-Posten, a serial number uncovered during restoration in 2026 matched the number recorded in correspondence about Autry’s guitar in 1932. The correspondence confirmed that Gene Autry had purchased and owned the guitar.Swedish woman discovered a rare Martin guitar among her father's belongingsSandra discovered the instrument among the possessions of her late father, Owe, in Gullspång, a small town in rural Sweden. He had been a musician and guitar collector, leaving behind around 25 guitars. However, he had never mentioned this particular instrument. In 2021, Sandra brought it to guitar collector and valuer Leif Lundbäck in Gothenburg.She had nearly sold it for 500 kronor, but a potential buyer advised her to have it valued first. Lundbäck identified it as a Martin OM-45 made in the early 1930s. He recognised the model as exceptionally rare and began investigating the name engraved on its fretboard, which someone had tried to cover with black paint.How a missing Hollywood star's guitar was discovered in SwedenThe name on the fretboard led Lundbäck to Gene Autry, the country singer and Hollywood star. He contacted representatives of Autry’s museum in California and sent photographs of the instrument. Dick Boak, who worked for Martin for 40 years and used its archives, compared the Swedish guitar with a photograph of Autry holding an OM-45.He said the grain of the guitar’s top matched. The serial number found inside the body had been sanded away, however, so the connection could not yet be established with certainty. Representatives of Autry's widow, Jackie, offered $20,000 for the guitar, saying she wanted to donate it to Autry's museum.Restoration uncovers the secret behind Gene Autry's missing guitarThe guitar remained unresolved for years. Sandra was reluctant to sell it or take further action after receiving a warning from representatives of Autry’s widow. In 2025, she asked Lundbäck for help, and he contacted restorer Andras Novak. During restoration in 2026, Novak separated the guitar’s neck from its body and noticed five digits that had been concealed.He recognised them as a serial number. The number matched the one in letters exchanged between Martin and a Chicago music shop in the 1930s, when Autry’s guitar was sent for repair. Historian and Martin expert Greig Historian and Martin expert Greig Hutton examined the number and confirmed that it was the same. It settled a question about the instrument’s identity.The guitar's ownership remains disputed between Sandra and Autry's widowThe serial number confirms this is the OM-45 Autry owned in the early 1930s. Whether it was stolen is still unproven. Sandra has questioned whether it was stolen, saying it might have been sold or given away.She inherited it from her father, who was born decades after the reported theft. Jackie Autry wants the guitar donated to the Autry Museum, while Sandra has not agreed to hand it over. The dispute has yet to reach a clear resolution.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports about the discovery of Gene Autry's missing guitar in Sweden, its identification through historical records, and the ongoing dispute over its ownership. The Times of India has not independently verified the circumstances surrounding its reported theft in 1932, how it reached Sweden or the competing ownership claims.You use AI every day. articles.title: Butter chicken in space: China prepares halal feast for Pakistan’s first astronaut
articles.summary: Butter chicken, beef nihari, lamb korma, and curried chickpeas (chole) have entered Earth’s orbit aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.
articles.body: Butter chicken, beef nihari, lamb korma, and curried chickpeas (chole) have entered Earth’s orbit aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft. The dishes were specifically picked for Pakistan’s first astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, aboard China’s Tiangong space station, making sure his first taste of life in orbit feels a little like home.Ali became the first foreign astronaut to enter China’s space station on Wednesday, arriving aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft with Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi. The crew was welcomed by the three astronauts already aboard Tiangong, bringing the station’s population to six during the crew handover.The China Astronaut Research and Training Centre prepared the food selection to accommodate Ali’s dietary requirements, drawing on South Asian food culture and halal standards. Researchers developed seven Pakistani-style space foods, with beef nihari, lamb korma, butter chicken and curried chickpeas among the dishes identified in reports by Chinese state media.The recipes were designed to meet astronauts’ nutritional needs while retaining familiar flavours. Researchers considered Ali’s preference for spices such as turmeric and curry, and repeatedly tested and refined the meals before finalising them. The food production process followed halal requirements, according to reports by CGTN.The menu also reflects a change of taste during Ali’s preparations in China. The original plan included Pakistani spiced milk tea, but after developing a liking for Chinese black tea and rice, Ali requested more of those items for his spaceflight. They were added to the food arrangements.A special dinner for the six astronauts was planned as the two crews met aboard the station, with dishes selected for both Chinese and Pakistani tastes. Tiangong has previously made a feature of shared meals between crews, including a barbecue prepared in a hot-air oven during an earlier mission.Ali, a serving Pakistan Air Force officer, lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwestern China on Wednesday alongside Tang and Wu. The spacecraft docked with Tiangong a few hours after launch, and the hatches were opened later that day, allowing the Shenzhou-24 crew to join their colleagues.During his introduction to the Chinese astronauts, Ali recited a couplet by celebrated Pakistani poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal, known as the Poet of the East.“Beyond the stars are even more worlds, there are still even more tests of passion,” he said, later translating the couplet for his crewmates.Ali said he was “incredibly excited” to become the first foreign astronaut aboard the Chinese space station.“A childhood dream has finally come true,” he said.Beyond the welcome and the special menu, Ali’s short stay will focus on scientific research. He is expected to work on experiments from Pakistan in life sciences and materials science, including studies of cyanobacteria growth and carbon dioxide absorption in microgravity, the resilience of quinoa seeds exposed to space conditions, graphene-based composite protection and the repair performance of self-healing carbon-fibre composites.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'We were told he was under no investigation': JD Vance on Nvidia CEO Huang amid China spy claims
articles.summary: JD Vance speaks out on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, stating he is not under investigation after links to Chinese intelligence claims. Vance criticizes the use of anonymous sources in allegations affecting careers.
articles.body: US Vice President JD Vance has said federal officials assured him that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation, pushing back against concerns over reports linking Huang to a woman suspected of having connections with Chinese intelligence.Speaking to CNN's Kit Maher at a pre-Thanksgiving meal for US troops in Dayton, Ohio, on Wednesday, Vance said he had received assurances from Attorney General Todd Blanche and other government officials that there was no investigation involving Huang.“We were told that he was under no investigation,” Vance said. He added that allegations against the Nvidia chief were based on anonymous reporting rather than evidence.Vance also criticised the use of anonymous sources to make allegations that could affect someone's professional position. He said people should not lose their jobs over claims that were not supported by concrete evidence.“I talked to the attorney general. I talked to other folks as well,” Vance told CNN, referring to the assurances he had received from officials in the administration.Blanche had also dismissed questions about whether Huang had been investigated. When asked about the matter on Tuesday, the attorney general responded, “For what?”Vance's remarks follow a series of public statements from senior Trump administration officials defending Huang and rejecting suggestions that the Nvidia chief or the company had been involved in wrongdoing. President Donald Trump has also backed Huang.Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as president and chief executive officer on Monday, following his departure amid reports about his alleged extramarital affairs and claims that a woman linked to him was suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence.In its announcement, Nvidia said the board had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after discussions and meetings with him. It said directors were satisfied with his candour and ability to lead the company.The board also said it had received input from senior US government officials and was confident that Huang's reinstatement did not pose a national security risk.“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” chairman Harvey C Jones said.Nvidia also confirmed that an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort would continue. The board had formed a committee comprising independent directors and appointed external legal counsel to assist with the probe. Huang has expressed support for the investigation and committed to cooperating with it.The company has also established a separate National Security and Export Control Committee, made up entirely of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. It said the committee would work with legal counsel and specialist advisers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Japan travel warning: UK embassy flags drink-spiking, credit card fraud targeting tourists in Tokyo
articles.summary: The British embassy in Tokyo has launched an online awareness campaign warning tourists from the UK about rising cases of drink-spiking and credit card
articles.body: The British embassy in Tokyo has launched an online awareness campaign warning tourists from the UK about rising cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud in Japan, particularly in popular nightlife districts of the Japanese capital.The campaign features British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, who cautions visitors against being lured into bars by strangers offering to introduce them to English-speaking women. Victims are allegedly served drinks mixed with drugs before large sums are charged to their credit cards while they are unconscious.In a video released as part of the campaign, Dow acknowledges that Japan is generally a safe destination but warns tourists against becoming complacent. He says young men travelling alone are particularly vulnerable to such scams.According to the British newspaper The Independent, cases involving British tourists have increased since 2024, with some victims reportedly losing as much as £35,000 (around $46,000) in a single night without remembering what happened."Stay alert, trust your gut, keep an eye on your stuff and don't follow strangers into bars," Dow advises in the video.UK issues warning over nightlife scams in JapanThe campaign follows an advisory issued by the UK's Foreign Office earlier this year, which flagged an increase in reports of drink-spiking and credit card fraud targeting visitors to Japan.According to the advisory, tourists have been approached by English-speaking street touts, locally known as Kyakuhiki, who persuade them to enter bars and nightclubs.The Foreign Office has cautioned visitors against following such touts into establishments, highlighting the risks in popular entertainment districts across Japan.Tokyo police have identified areas including Roppongi, Shibuya, Kabukicho and Ikebukuro as locations where tourists face a higher risk of such crimes.Tokyo police arrest five after nightclub raidsJapanese authorities have stepped up action against establishments accused of defrauding customers.Earlier this month, police conducted 160 pre-dawn raids in Tokyo and arrested five people linked to two establishments in the Kabukicho entertainment district following complaints that customers had been overcharged.Police recorded 340 cases of street touts defrauding customers in the Shinjuku area between January and October, compared with 195 cases during the corresponding period last year, according to the Asahi Shimbun newspaper.The Guardian reported that victims collectively paid around 390 million yen, with foreign nationals accounting for approximately 70 per cent of those targeted.In one reported case, a customer was allegedly charged 9.6 million yen (around $60,000) on a credit card.A senior police investigator told the newspaper that reported cases could represent only a fraction of the actual incidents, as some tourists discover the fraud only after returning home or leave Japan without reporting the crime.Japan tourism boom draws record foreign visitorsThe warning comes as Japan continues to attract record numbers of international visitors.The country welcomed 42.7 million foreign tourists last year, crossing the 40-million mark for the first time. Among them were approximately 530,000 visitors from the UK.The growing number of international tourists has also brought increased attention to scams and criminal activity targeting visitors, particularly in busy nightlife districts.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Modi is sitting quietly today’: Kharge hints at BJP top brass rift, jibes at Yogi over PM ambitions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday credited the people of Uttar Pradesh with checking the BJP's electoral ambitions in the 2024
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday credited the people of Uttar Pradesh with checking the BJP's electoral ambitions in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying their verdict had forced Prime Minister Narendra Modi to go quiet on his '400 paar' slogan.Addressing a 'Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan' at the Congress office in Lucknow on Constitution Day, Kharge also accused the BJP of allowing its funds to swell while inflation, unemployment and the prices of cooking gas and essential food items continued to rise."I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, 'Abki Baar, 400 Paar' (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today," Kharge said.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won 36 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections.Kharge also claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah had reduced his public statements, adding, "I do not know whether the two (Modi and Shah) are getting along or not."In a veiled reference to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, the Congress chief said another leader in Lucknow also had his eyes on the prime minister's chair.Kharge questions BJP's Rs 10,000 crore fundsTargeting the BJP over its finances, Kharge questioned the source of nearly Rs 10,000 crore in party funds, alleging that the ruling party was benefiting from the use of central investigative agencies to intimidate people and collect money."Everything has become expensive. But the BJP's coffers are filling up. Where has the BJP got Rs 10,000 crore in its party funds from? You question us, but we want to ask you where this Rs 10,000 crore came from," he said.The BJP has cash and deposits worth nearly Rs 10,000 crore, according to its annual audit report recently submitted to the Election Commission.Kharge alleged that the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Income Tax Department and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were being used to threaten people and extract money."By deploying the ED, Income Tax Department and CBI to threaten people and extract money, the BJP is filling its coffers. This is nothing short of robbery," he said.Congress holds Constitution Day march in LucknowThe Congress organised a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Lucknow on Thursday to mark Constitution Day. However, the march did not reach its intended destination, with Kharge alleging that the state government was afraid of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.Kharge said the government had begun fearing even the party's shadows and asserted that Congress workers would take out the march whenever an opportunity arose.Kharge also recalled the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, and highlighted Uttar Pradesh's contribution to the process. He referred to a resolution passed by the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly in October 1937 calling for the repeal of the Government of India Act, 1935, and the framing of India's Constitution by an elected Constituent Assembly.Earlier, Kharge paid tribute to the ashes of BR Ambedkar at the Ambedkar Mahasabha in Lucknow before heading to the Congress office. Congress state president Aradhana Misra Mona, MP Imran Masood and the party's state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam were among those present.Meanwhile, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused the Modi government of undermining parliamentary democracy and disregarding parliamentary conventions. Addressing reporters during the march, he said the party was holding protests at state headquarters across the country over concerns about Parliament's functioning and the protection of the Constitution."They have turned Parliament into a complete mockery; even after 106 days, they haven't even prorogued Parliament," Venugopal said, questioning the delay in convening the Winter Session.He also alleged that the government had denied people an opportunity to observe Constitution Day through parliamentary proceedings, and asked why there was no indication of when the Winter Session would begin.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Single-digit parties': Punjab Congress president takes a dig at BJP-SAD alliance
articles.summary: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Thursday took a swipe at the newly announced Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance, predicting that the two
articles.body: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Thursday took a swipe at the newly announced Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance, predicting that the two parties would together win only single-digit seats in the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.Reacting to the SAD-BJP alliance, Pargat Singh said, "These are strictly single-digit parties; even together, both will end up in single digits."He further said that people in Punjab were still unhappy with the BJP and SAD over their role during the farmers' protest against the now-repealed farm laws, ANI reported.Referring to the farmers' agitation, Pargat Singh claimed that around 750 farmers had lost their lives during the protest.He also targeted the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling it the "East India Company" and ruling out any possibility of the Congress joining hands with the party."They (AAP) are the East India Company, and the Congress never shakes hands with any East India Company," Singh said.Launching a further attack on AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and his associates, he said, "These are thugs, Kejriwal and company."The Congress leader's remarks came amid renewed political activity in Punjab ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The SAD and BJP, which ended their alliance in 2020 over the Centre's farm laws, have now joined hands again.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Samsung Display partners with ams OSRAM for microLED technology
articles.summary: Samsung Display has signed an investment agreement to acquire a 9.1% equity interest in ams OSRAM for approximately EUR 210 million ($230.39 million).
articles.body: Samsung Display has signed an investment agreement to acquire a 9.1% equity interest in ams OSRAM for approximately EUR 210 million ($230.39 million). Under the agreement, Samsung Display will acquire 9,984,439 newly issued shares of ams OSRAM and is expected to become its largest shareholder upon closing. Separately, the two companies have also entered into a strategic partnership to jointly develop next-generation ultra-small microLED technology for display applications. Through this collaboration, Samsung Display plans to step up research and development to accelerate the potential commercialization of ultra-small microLED technology, including efforts to improve its efficiency and cost competitiveness.With more than 120 years of history, ams OSRAM has extensive technological expertise in advanced epitaxy, LED miniaturization and high-volume LED manufacturing, as well as high-density integration. Through its investment in ams OSRAM, Samsung Display plans to extend its world-leading technological expertise in OLED to inorganic self-emissive technologies. In particular, the company plans to evaluate the performance and applicability of ultra-small LEDs manufactured by ams OSRAM and establish the manufacturing processes and production technologies needed to commercialize next-generation ultra-small microLED displays.The company will also explore mid- to long-term business opportunities across a wide range of applications, from ultra-small to ultra-large displays.Samsung Display expects to complete the share acquisition in early 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including applicable regulatory approvals.“This partnership marks a major strategic milestone for ams OSRAM. It creates a funded pathway for a novel next-generation ultra-small microLED technology from technology development towards potential industrialization, while Samsung Display’s strategic investment in ams OSRAM underscores our shared commitment to its successful development and commercialization,” said Aldo Kamper, CEO of ams OSRAM.“Ultra-small microLED is a next-generation inorganic self-emissive technology with the potential to overcome the limitations of existing technologies in areas such as brightness and lifetime. Its potential is not limited to any particular product category, but extends across an exceptionally broad range of applications, from ultra-small to ultra-large displays,” said Chung Yi, President and CEO of Samsung Display.“This investment reflects our determination not to remain complacent with where we are today, but to proactively respond to technological evolution and emerging market demand while securing new engines for future growth,” Yi added.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: PDA quota, dole for jobless, caste survey: Decoding Akhilesh Yadav's big manifesto promises for UP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Twenty-five lakh government jobs, Rs 5,000 a month for unemployed graduates, and 50 per cent reservation for the PDA communities in government
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Twenty-five lakh government jobs, Rs 5,000 a month for unemployed graduates, and 50 per cent reservation for the PDA communities in government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore. Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections is an ambitious, on-paper bid to build a winning coalition of voters against the BJP government led by chief minister Yogi Adityanath.Unveiled on Constitution Day, 'Sattais Ka Sankalp: PDA Ka Pran Patra – Jan-Man Ka Manifesto 2027' has placed Akhilesh's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formula at its core. After losing back-to-back assembly elections in 2017 and 2022, the SP is seeking to expand beyond its traditional Yadav-Muslim support base by combining caste-based representation with welfare promises for youth, women, and farmers.The PDA arithmeticFocusing on SP's social justice pitch, the manifesto promises a statewide caste census and 50 per cent reservation for Dalit and PDA communities in government contracts. It has also promised a Dalit development council headed by the CM and 20 per cent of the state budget for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe welfare.The party has also promised a special recruitment drive to fill reserved vacancies and Samajwadi canteens offering meals at Rs 5 to women, poor people and PDA communities.The promises are aimed at giving backward and Dalit communities a greater stake in government jobs, contracts and welfare spending. They also reflect Akhilesh's attempt to expand the SP's traditional support base beyond Yadavs.Non-Yadav OBCs make up an estimated 33 per cent of the electorate, compared with around 8 per cent for Yadavs. Spanning Kurmis, Lodhs, Kushwahas, Jats, Rajbhars, Nishads and Most Backward Classes, these communities have been an important pillar of the BJP's electoral expansion since 2014.Yadavs, meanwhile, remain the SP's most reliable support base. Akhilesh's challenge is to expand into non-Yadav OBC communities without alienating his traditional voters.The caste census promise is central to this effort. By seeking to establish the population and socio-economic status of different communities, the SP wants to make representation and distribution of resources key electoral issues.The party is seeking to bridge the divide between Jatav and non-Jatav Dalits, a constituency that has been central to the BJP's expansion in Uttar Pradesh.The Muslim factorThe SP has placed Muslim outreach within its broader PDA framework, promising constitutional protection, equality, employment opportunities and representation rather than announcing a separate cash-transfer scheme for the community.The prominent presence given to senior leader Azam Khan at the manifesto launch in Lucknow was also a political signal, reinforcing the party's effort to retain its Muslim support base.Muslims account for around 19 per cent of UP's electorate and have a significant presence in 143 of the state's 403 assembly constituencies. Their estimated population share exceeds 30 per cent in 73 seats, rising to 60-65 per cent in Rampur Nagar and 55-58 per cent in Chamrauwa. Another 70 constituencies have a Muslim population share of 20-30 per cent, concentrated largely in Rohilkhand and western UP.The SP's calculation is to secure Muslim consolidation while expanding the PDA coalition to other communities. The challenge is to do so without giving the BJP an opening to turn the contest into one of religious polarisation.25 lakh jobs, Rs 5,000 allowance: The Gen-Z pitchTwenty-five lakh government jobs over five years, another two to three crore employment opportunities in other sectors and a monthly allowance of Rs 5,000 for unemployed graduates are at the centre of the SP's youth-focused pitch.The party has proposed an annual calendar for government vacancies, with recruitment processes involving single-stage examinations to be completed within three months and those involving multiple stages within six months. It has also promised a system free of paper leaks, with officials and ministers to be held personally accountable for irregularities.To revive a signature scheme from its 2012-17 tenure, the SP has promised free laptops for students passing Class 12. Other education commitments include reopening 26,000 primary schools, increasing the monthly honorarium of Shiksha Mitras by Rs 5,000 until their regularisation process is completed, and providing Wi-Fi facilities in schools.The party has also pitched technology-led growth, citing the establishment of HCL's facility and an IT City in Lucknow during its previous government."Delivering on the aspirations of Gen-Z and Gen Alpha will be part of our commitment," Akhilesh said at the manifesto launch.The focus on young voters is significant. Those aged 18-29 accounted for 22.9% of the electorate, or around 3.44 crore voters, in the 2022 assembly elections.By foregrounding recruitment delays, paper leaks and unemployment, the SP is seeking to turn the concerns of this sizeable constituency into an electoral challenge for the Yogi Adityanath government.For 'aadhi aabadi'An annual pension of Rs 40,000 for elderly women, including elderly women artisans, 33 per cent representation for women in new police recruitments and stronger surveillance in public places are among the SP's key promises to women.The party has also announced a separate women-centric manifesto and proposed CCTV cameras, drone surveillance and dedicated cybercrime units in every district.The pitch comes against the backdrop of the BJP's efforts to consolidate women voters through welfare delivery, including free rations, housing and cooking gas connections.Women have emerged as an increasingly important electoral constituency, and the SP's challenge is to persuade them that its proposed financial assistance and safety measures offer a credible alternative to the BJP's welfare delivery and law-and-order pitch.Relief promise across the rural beltAn immediate farm loan waiver, a legal guarantee for minimum support prices (MSP) on 23 crops and milk, free electricity for agricultural irrigation and up to 300 units of free power for rural domestic consumers form the core of the SP's agricultural package.The party has also promised a price compensation mechanism for crops such as potatoes, tomatoes and onions that fall outside the MSP system. A Rs 15,000-crore corpus would be created to ensure sugarcane farmers receive payments within 24 hours, while sugarcane prices would be increased annually based on the actual cost of cultivation. The SP has also proposed Rs 1.5 lakh crore for rural infrastructure.The package seeks to appeal to farmers across caste groups, particularly in agricultural and sugarcane-growing regions.The rural constituency is electorally significant. Of UP's 403 Assembly seats, 222 are classified as rural and another 131 as semi-urban in the constituency data used for this analysis. Together, they account for the overwhelming majority of the state's seats.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India's first museum dedicated to Chief Justices of India inaugurated at OP Jindal Global University in Sonipat
articles.summary: India's first museum dedicated to the Chief Justices of India was inaugurated at OP Jindal Global University (JGU) in Sonipat on Wednesday, with 10 former
articles.body: India's first museum dedicated to the Chief Justices of India was inaugurated at OP Jindal Global University (JGU) in Sonipat on Wednesday, with 10 former Chief Justices of India attending the event in person or virtually.The museum, inaugurated on the eve of Constitution Day, documents the lives and contributions of former Chief Justices and traces the evolution of the Supreme Court and India's constitutional framework.It has been set up across five galleries, featuring more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 High Courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive biographical pillars and displays on 20 landmark judgments.The inauguration was attended by former Chief Justices MN Venkatachaliah, BN Kirpal, S Rajendra Babu, KG Balakrishnan, P Sathasivam, RM Lodha, Dipak Misra, Sharad A Bobde, UU Lalit and BR Gavai.The event was held ahead of Constitution Day, observed on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.Museum traces history of Supreme Court and constitutional lawAccording to the university, the museum seeks to present the office of the Chief Justice as an institution central to constitutional governance, while documenting the people, decisions and debates that have shaped the judiciary.Its exhibits include a holographic courtroom, artworks, sculptures and installations, alongside biographical displays and recordings of former judges.Former Chief Justice MN Venkatachaliah said the rule of law and democratic freedoms had played an important role in India's progress. He said the museum could contribute to legal education and help prepare future practitioners.Former CJI BR Gavai said the museum documented the work of successive Chief Justices as well as the Supreme Court's contribution to constitutional law over the past 76 years. He also spoke about the Constitution's emphasis on inclusion and representation, referring to the participation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, minorities and women in public institutions.Former CJI UU Lalit said the museum traced the development of jurisprudence alongside the country's growth. He said the evolution of law was closely connected with economic development and the well-being of the population.Former CJI Sharad A Bobde spoke about the responsibility of the judiciary to uphold the rule of law and recalled the Supreme Court's functioning during the Covid pandemic, including the introduction of online hearings.Former CJI RM Lodha said the museum's displays included judgments that had shaped India's constitutional framework. He referred to the development of public interest litigation and the basic structure doctrine, while also acknowledging that the judiciary had faced periods of difficulty.Former CJI P Sathasivam said the Supreme Court had grown in importance since it began functioning in January 1950. He identified independence from the executive, integrity and transparency as essential to maintaining public confidence in the institution.Former CJI Dipak Misra said the museum could help students understand constitutional values, including liberty, equality and fraternity. Former CJI S. Rajendra Babu said the exhibits would be useful to law scholars and researchers by helping them understand the evolution of the judiciary and the issues it had addressed.Former CJI KG Balakrishnan urged law students to study the Constitution and understand their responsibilities as future legal professionals.Former CJI BN Kirpal also participated in the proceedings.Five galleries feature judgments, judicial history and artworksThe museum is organised into five galleries: Pathways of Justice, Pillars of Justice, Hall of Constitutional Voices, Keystones of Justice and Ideas of Justice.Pathways of Justice explores the historical and social foundations of justice through 10 marble plaques recalling trials from colonial India.Its artworks address themes such as untouchability, dowry, bonded labour, education, transparency, workplace dignity and climate justice. The gallery also features a model of the Supreme Court and a display titled 'Branches of Justice'.Pillars of Justice focuses on the lives of former Chief Justices through 20 interactive pillars, each equipped with four screens. It also features 22 regional handloom tapestries representing the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, along with models of 25 High Courts.Hall of Constitutional Voices presents recordings of 11 figures associated with India's constitutional history. It also includes an oral history project featuring conversations with former Chief Justices and other senior judges.Keystones of Justice examines 20 landmark judgments and the principles behind them. Its exhibits include a holographic courtroom and an installation titled 'From Paper to Precedent', made using ceramics, paper and jute.Ideas of Justice features a sculpture garden and busts of judges. Its installations include 'The Robe of Justice' and 'The Right to Fly', which refers to JGU founding chancellor Naveen Jindal's legal battle over citizens' right to fly the national flag.Jindal said the museum extended the university's existing Constitution Museum by focusing on the Supreme Court's role in upholding constitutional values. JGU founding vice-chancellor C. Raj Kumar said the project aimed to bring together law, history, memory and public engagement to document the institution's constitutional role.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
